extracted_notes.text: According to an academic article by Cody Kommers and five other scholars that was published in January 2026, AI slop has "so far resisted formal definition."

Although they argue it is impossible to precisely describe a boundary between slop and non-slop, Kommers et. al. identify three "prototypical properties" that characterise AI slop: superficial competence, asymmetric effort and mass producibility.

Three main "dimensions of variance", or ways in which AI slop can vary, are its instrumental utility (why was it created?), the level of personalization (is it so specific as to only be interesting to one person or a small friend group?) and the level of surrealism, where some AI slop is "ludicrously implausible" while other slop is more realistic.

Art curator Francesco D'Isa considers it wrong to say that AI "produces only slop", and sees the majority of human production as having "always been slop", with the canon of art being "the surviving tip of an immense iceberg of forgotten, derivative, or simply boring creations".

All entity profiles and unique quotes were retained to ensure a diverse visual experience.

blocks.rationale: Introductory hook to set the stage for the theoretical discussion of AI slop.
blocks.text_content: While the term **AI slop** has become a common pejorative for low-quality synthetic media, scholars are finding that pinning down a precise definition is surprisingly difficult. As the technology evolves, the line between a useful tool and digital clutter becomes increasingly blurred.

blocks.rationale: Introduces the key figures providing theoretical frameworks for AI slop.
Transitions from the general perspectives to the specific difficulty of formal definition.
blocks.text_content: The challenge lies in the fact that slop isn't a single type of content, but rather a spectrum of quality and intent. This ambiguity is highlighted by researchers who note that the concept has remained elusive to academic categorization.

blocks.rationale: Introduces the specific academic finding regarding the lack of a formal definition.
blocks.text_content: In early 2026, a group of scholars attempted to formalize the concept. Their findings suggest that AI slop is less of a distinct category and more of a perceived quality of content.

blocks.text_content: Rather than a strict definition, scholars identify three **prototypical properties** that act as hallmarks of AI slop. These traits explain why certain content feels 'off' or low-effort even when it looks polished.

blocks.rationale: Visually represents the three core characteristics of AI slop.
Transitions to the idea that slop varies across different dimensions.
blocks.text_content: While these properties provide a baseline, not all slop is created equal. The nature of the content often shifts based on the goal of the creator and the intended audience.

blocks.rationale: Introduces the concept of dimensions of variance to explain the diversity of slop.
blocks.text_content: To better understand the variety of AI-generated clutter, researchers look at **dimensions of variance**. These are the specific ways in which slop can differ from one instance to another, ranging from its purpose to its plausibility.

blocks.rationale: Uses an accordion to detail the three dimensions of variance: utility, personalization, and surrealism.
Moves the conversation from academic frameworks to a broader art-historical perspective.
blocks.text_content: These frameworks help us categorize the 'what' and 'how' of AI slop, but some argue that the phenomenon isn't entirely new—it's simply a new medium for an old human habit.

blocks.rationale: Introduces Francesco D'Isa's perspective on human production vs. AI slop.
blocks.text_content: Art curator **Francesco D'Isa** offers a provocative counter-argument. He suggests that the tendency to produce low-quality, derivative work is not unique to AI, but has been a constant in human creativity throughout history.

blocks.rationale: Highlights D'Isa's metaphor regarding the canon of art and the 'iceberg' of slop.
Concluding thought that synthesizes the academic and artistic views.
blocks.text_content: From this perspective, AI slop is not a new category of failure, but an acceleration of the vast amount of mediocre content that has always existed. The only difference now is the *scale* and *speed* at which the iceberg is growing.
